body.working_title: What error measures reward: simulations of RMSE, MAE, MAPE and sMAPE

body.text: Brief requirements (the supervisor, 2026-11-14): (1) a study separate from the review entrylib:2026.000008, supporting its claims; (2) simulations with simple models; (3) the measures MAE, RMSE, MAPE and sMAPE; (4) what each measure recommends: the point forecast or method it selects; (5) a variety of situations; (6) a plan and hypotheses, recorded with claimset lab. The script lines that meet each are listed once the script exists.

Which point forecasts and which forecasting methods do RMSE, MAE, MAPE and sMAPE select when outcomes are symmetric, skewed or intermittent, and when series differ in scale, and do their choices agree with the claims of the review entrylib:2026.000008@v2?

body.definition: Root mean squared error of point forecasts over the outcomes they are evaluated on: sqrt(mean((y - f)^2)).
Mean absolute error of point forecasts: mean(|y - f|).
Mean absolute percentage error: 100 * mean(|y - f| / |y|), over outcomes y other than zero; the number of outcomes left out for y = 0 is reported.
Symmetric mean absolute percentage error, in the form of the M3 and M4 competitions: 200 * mean(|y - f| / (|y| + |f|)); a pair with y = f = 0 is left out and counted.
Root mean squared scaled error of a series: its RMSE divided by the in-sample RMSE of the one-step naive forecast of that series.
Of a grid of candidate point forecasts, the one with the lowest value of a measure over the simulated outcomes, expressed as a multiple of the median of the outcome distribution (1 = the median).

Outcomes are drawn from a known distribution; each candidate point forecast on a fine grid (multiples of the distribution's median) is scored by each measure on the same draws; the measure's selected forecast is the candidate with the lowest score. Repeated over independent replications with their own seeds.
Outcomes drawn from a normal distribution with mean 100 and standard deviation 10: symmetric, so mean and median coincide.
Outcomes y = exp(x), x normal with mean log(100) and standard deviation s, for s in {0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1}: positive and right-skewed; median 100, mean 100 exp(s^2 / 2).
Counts drawn from a negative binomial distribution with mean 0.3, 0.5 or 0.6 and size 1: more than half of them are zero, so the median is zero while the mean is positive.
Series of 120 observations with log y_t = l_t + e_t, l_t = l_{t-1} + u_t, e_t ~ N(0, s^2), u_t ~ N(0, (0.3 s)^2), l_0 = log(100), s in {0.25, 0.5}; the last 12 observations are held out and forecast.

Simple exponential smoothing fitted to log y by the smoothing parameter alpha in {0.05, 0.10, ..., 0.95} with the lowest in-sample one-step sum of squared errors; its level l_T forecasts every horizon h. The median forecast is exp(l_T); the mean forecast is exp(l_T + v_h / 2), with v_h = sigma^2 (1 + (h - 1) alpha^2) the h-step variance of the log forecast error and sigma^2 the in-sample one-step error variance.
A point forecast that targets the mean of the outcome's distribution.
A point forecast that targets the median of the outcome's distribution.

body.term: collection of series on different scales
body.definition: Sets of 20 series of the multiplicative local level kind with s = 0.25, of which 19 start at level 100 and one at level 10,000, forecast by two methods that differ on the large series from how they differ on the others.

body.text: Each hypothesis tests a claim of the review entrylib:2026.000008@v2: H1 tests C2; H2 tests C7; H3 tests C4; H4 tests C5; H5 tests C6; H6 tests C8; H7 tests C2; H8 tests C7; H9 tests C25; H10 tests C26. The hypotheses restate those claims as what a measure selects under known distributions or simulated series, so that the simulations can support or refute them.

body.definition: Symmetric mean absolute percentage error, in the form of the M3 and M4 competitions: 200 * mean of |y - f| / (|y| + |f|) over the outcomes, where a pair with y = f (including y = f = 0) contributes 0, so that the measure is defined for every pair (the supervisor's rule, 2026-11-14).

Counts of which more than 50% are zero, so that the median is zero while the mean is positive: negative binomial with size 1 and mean 0.3, 0.5 or 0.6 (zeros 77%, 67%, 62%), and Poisson with lambda 0.3, 0.5 or 0.65 (zeros 74%, 61%, 52%). Each run reports the share of zeros it drew.
Counts drawn from a Poisson distribution with lambda 1.5, 3.5 or 10 (fewer than half zero), whose mean is lambda and whose median is the smallest integer m with P(y <= m) >= 0.5 (1, 3 and 10).

body.text: The supervisor's changes to the design, 2026-11-14, before any run: intermittent outcomes are defined by more than 50% zeros; sMAPE scores a pair with y = f as 0; the sMAPE hypothesis is about the mean (H13), with a second about the median (H14); a hypothesis that sMAPE selects zero on intermittent outcomes (H15, the supervisor's expectation); Poisson outcomes are added; every decision rule uses 99% confidence intervals (1% level), not p-values; SES on logs is kept. The MAPE hypothesis stays about the median (H16): on lognormal outcomes the median lies below the mean, so a forecast below the median is below the mean too, the stronger test of the claim that MAPE suits neither.

body.definition: The naive forecast: the last observation, for every horizon.

Simple exponential smoothing on the original scale with the smoothing parameter fixed at 0.1, the level started at the first observation: l_t = l_{t-1} + 0.1 (y_t - l_{t-1}); its last level forecasts every horizon.

body.term: collection of series on different scales
body.definition: Sets of 20 series of 120 observations, the last 12 held out: 19 small series with log y_t = l_t + e_t, l_t = l_{t-1} + u_t, e_t ~ N(0, 0.25^2), u_t ~ N(0, 0.075^2), l_0 = log(100); and one large series, a random walk in logs, log y_t = log y_{t-1} + w_t, w_t ~ N(0, 0.05^2), log y_0 = log(10000). The naive forecast and SES with alpha 0.1 are expected to rank differently on the large series from the small ones.
